correctness.rationale: Canonical ladder operators give J_N=B_N^*B_N; the exact determinant recurrence at x=1 is t^(N-1)(t-N). The full number operator has spectrum 0,1,... and strict finite-section min--max gives all other Ritz eigenvalues >1, fixing the direction of the crossing. Bidiagonal inversion and a binomial convolution give the exact inverse trace. Poisson concentration plus a harmonic upper bound on the nonminimal reciprocal eigenvalues gives the full subcritical prefactor and relative O_rho(1/N) remainder. A singular-value lower bound and a top-edge discrete sine vector give the supercritical limit. An extracted standalone checker passed 250 supplementary assertions of finite identities and trends; asymptotic claims are analytic, not computational extrapolations.

value.rationale: The first N Hermite vectors are the canonical finite spectral approximation of a displaced oscillator. The exact critical crossing t=N, sharp exponentially small first-zero prefactor for t=rho N< N, and supercritical linear edge when t=rho N>N form a natural complete outer-regime phase diagram with a concrete approximation-stability interpretation. The reciprocal trace is reusable for eigenvalue estimates. The result is not an arbitrary finite sample or a textbook fixed-parameter limit, and it explicitly excludes the unresolved critical window.
